headline: Historic win: Bangladesh beats Australia by 9 wickets in Darwin
summary: Bangladesh secures its first-ever Test victory on Australian soil, marking a monumental achievement in the nation's cricketing history.
details: Bangladesh achieved a historic milestone by defeating Australia by nine wickets in Darwin, marking their first-ever Test win on Australian soil. The match concluded inside four days, representing a dominant performance against one of the world's strongest teams.
The victory was built on a strong foundation laid by fast bowler Hasan Mahmud, who took a career-best 6-55 to bowl Australia out for 198 on the opening day.
Tanzid Hasan led the batting charge with his maiden Test century, supported by crucial contributions from captain Najmul Hossain Shanto and all-rounder Mehidy Hasan Miraz.
The result was particularly surprising as Bangladesh had been bowled out for just 54 in a warm-up match against a Cricket Australia XI just days prior.
Former captain Akram Khan called it the biggest achievement for Bangladesh cricket in Test matches, praising the complete team effort over individual brilliance.
BCB president Tamim Iqbal and former selector Abdur Razzak hailed the win as extraordinary, suggesting it strengthens Bangladesh's case for more Test opportunities against Australia.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman congratulated the team via video call, while fans described the victory as feeling like a national festival.
caption:
History made in Darwin! 🇧🇩
Bangladesh secures its first-ever Test victory on Australian soil with a crushing 9-wicket win.

Bangladesh achieved a historic milestone by defeating Australia by nine wickets in Darwin, marking their first-ever Test win on Australian soil. The match concluded inside four days, representing a dominant performance against one of the world's strongest teams.

The victory was built on a strong foundation laid by fast bowler Hasan Mahmud, who took a career-best 6-55 to bowl Australia out for 198 on the opening day.

Tanzid Hasan led the batting charge with his maiden Test century, supported by crucial contributions from captain Najmul Hossain Shanto and all-rounder Mehidy Hasan Miraz.

The result was particularly surprising as Bangladesh had been bowled out for just 54 in a warm-up match against a Cricket Australia XI just days prior.

Former captain Akram Khan called it the biggest achievement for Bangladesh cricket in Test matches, praising the complete team effort over individual brilliance.

BCB president Tamim Iqbal and former selector Abdur Razzak hailed the win as extraordinary, suggesting it strengthens Bangladesh's case for more Test opportunities against Australia.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman congratulated the team via video call, while fans described the victory as feeling like a national festival.

headline_marked: BRTC to [[roll out pink buses]] for women, operated by women
headline: BRTC to roll out pink buses for women, operated by women
summary: The new service will feature female drivers and conductors to provide a safer and more comfortable transport option for female passengers.
details: The Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation (BRTC) is launching a new fleet of pink buses dedicated exclusively to female passengers on Tuesday.
These buses will be operated by women drivers and conductors, ensuring a female-only environment for both staff and passengers.
The service will be inaugurated at the BRTC Dhaka Truck Depot in Tejgaon at 10:00 am on Tuesday.
The event will be attended by Road Transport and Bridges, Railways, and Shipping Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam as the chief guest.
Other special guests include Habibur Rashid, state minister for railways and road transport and highways, and Dr Mohammad Ziaul Haque, secretary of the Road Transport and Highways Division.
BRTC Chairman Abdul Latif Molla will chair the programme.
According to a BRTC press release, this initiative is part of the government's commitment to implement promises made in its election manifesto.
caption:
Women drivers, women conductors, and female-only passengers. BRTC is launching pink buses for women.

The Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation (BRTC) is launching a new fleet of pink buses dedicated exclusively to female passengers on Tuesday.

These buses will be operated by women drivers and conductors, ensuring a female-only environment for both staff and passengers.

The service will be inaugurated at the BRTC Dhaka Truck Depot in Tejgaon at 10:00 am on Tuesday.

The event will be attended by Road Transport and Bridges, Railways, and Shipping Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam as the chief guest.

Other special guests include Habibur Rashid, state minister for railways and road transport and highways, and Dr Mohammad Ziaul Haque, secretary of the Road Transport and Highways Division.

BRTC Chairman Abdul Latif Molla will chair the programme.

According to a BRTC press release, this initiative is part of the government's commitment to implement promises made in its election manifesto.
